definitions.explanation: Items bought at a travel destination to bring back as gifts or keepsakes. Encompasses food, crafts, and other local specialties typically sold at tourist spots and stations.

examples.japanese: {土産物|みやげもの}を{買|か}った。
{駅|えき}の{近|ちか}くに{土産物|みやげもの}{屋|や}がたくさんある。
examples.english: There are many souvenir shops near the station.

examples.japanese: この{地域|ちいき}の{土産物|みやげもの}として{最|もっと}も{人気|にんき}があるのは{地元|じもと}の{和菓子|わがし}だ。
examples.english: The most popular souvenir from this area is the local Japanese confectionery.

notes:
Composed of {土産|みやげ} (souvenir) and {物|もの} (thing, item). While お{土産|みやげ} refers to the gift or the concept of bringing gifts, {土産物|みやげもの} specifically refers to the goods themselves, especially as a commercial category. Often seen on signs for souvenir shops.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {土産物|みやげもの}{屋|や}: souvenir shop
- {土産物|みやげもの}{店|てん}: souvenir store
- {名物|めいぶつ}{土産物|みやげもの}: famous local souvenir
- {土産物|みやげもの}を{選|えら}ぶ: to choose souvenirs

SIMILAR WORDS:
- お{土産|みやげ}: souvenir, gift — the broader, everyday term; includes the social custom of bringing gifts
- {名産品|めいさんひん}: local specialty product — emphasizes regional fame; not necessarily bought as a gift
- {記念品|きねんひん}: memento, commemorative item — something kept as a personal memory rather than given as a gift
